---
applyTo: "Dockerfile,.dockerignore,.volcengine/**,.github/workflows/test.yml,.github/workflows/test-docker.yml,.github/workflows/deploy-main.yml"
---

Keep the workspace image based on Ubuntu 26.04 and build it for Linux amd64, the supported Linux architecture of the bundled Lynx runtime. Read Node and Rust versions from `.nvmrc` and `rust-toolchain.toml`, and keep the Corepack version aligned with `.github/actions/pnpm-install/action.yml`.

The public CP build has timed out connecting to both Ubuntu archive and security hosts over IPv4 as well as failing IPv6 connections; forcing IPv4 alone does not fix that failure. Pass `UBUNTU_MIRROR=http://mirrors.volces.com/ubuntu` as a build argument in CP, and apply the optional override to both stages' `/etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources`. Leave Ubuntu's default sources in place when the argument is unset. Preserve suites, components, and the Ubuntu signing keyring. Use `apt-get update --error-on=any` so a failed index download reports the actual network error instead of continuing to misleading package-not-found errors. CP's `buildkit-custom@3.0.0` ignores `--platform` in `buildParams`; use its default single-architecture Linux amd64 build and pass `--target runtime` there.

Build npm workspaces through the repository-root Turbo command used by `deploy-main.yml`, excluding both `benchx_cli` and `@lynx-js/benchmark-*`. Keep Wasm packages in this build. Exclude `swc_plugin_reactlynx`, `swc_plugin_reactlynx_compat`, and `web-core` only from the subsequent native Cargo build, and enable `ui_judge/server` to include its optional binary and packaged runtime assets.

Use separate builder and runtime stages. Keep only Node, production workspace dependencies, package outputs, and final native deliverables in the runtime image. Reinstall production dependencies with `--prefer-offline --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts` after removing workspace `node_modules`; do not rely on `pnpm prune` to prune a monorepo. Avoid `--offline`: a previous full install does not guarantee every package snapshot remains available for the production reinstall, so missing snapshots must be allowed to download. Preserve source files exported by workspace packages. Remove Cargo targets, build caches, and generated source maps before copying the workspace into the runtime stage. Copy both Rust executables, the React transform shared library, the generated launcher, the Lynx runtime library, and `lynx_core.js` explicitly. Strip only binaries built here, preserving the downloaded Lynx runtime unchanged. Do not copy compiler toolchains, package managers, headers, or download caches into the final image. Use BuildKit cache export `mode=min` so CI builds do not export intermediate builder layers.

Set runtime `LYNX_LIB_PATH` and `LYNX_CORE_JS_PATH` to the copied assets. The headless runner otherwise retains Cargo-injected paths into the SDK cache removed during cleanup.

Export production `node_modules` directories into a separate tree while preserving their workspace-relative paths and symlinks. Keep downloaded Lynx SDK files separate from Rust outputs. Use independent `COPY --link` layers for Node, production dependencies, the SDK, workspace files, and compiled Rust deliverables. Remove pnpm installation bookkeeping with variable timestamps and normalize exported timestamps, including symlinks, so unchanged file contents can produce reusable layers across commits. Do not remove source files used by package exports. Dependency splitting must preserve Node resolution through both pnpm links and workspace links. Exclude `.volcengine` from the runtime filesystem.

Do not copy host `node_modules`, Cargo targets, Turbo caches, or local environment files into the Docker build context. Validate the complete Dockerfile in the independent `test-docker.yml` workflow only for pull requests changing `.github/workflows/**`. Start without depending on the Ubuntu build, and keep Docker validation out of `test.yml` and its `done.needs`. Do not add push or merge-group triggers that would run this expensive build unconditionally. In GitHub Actions, build without pushing images, registry credentials, or `packages: write` permission. Do not build Docker images in `deploy-main.yml`. Pin Docker Actions to verified commit SHAs.

Keep Volcengine publishing in `.volcengine/pipeline.yml` and its custom step definition in `.volcengine/main-head.yml`. The pipeline only resolves main, fetches that commit, builds and uploads the image, and removes the checkout. Do not add registry retention scripts, post-build retagging, preflight checks, or pipeline test steps. Keep Dockerfile dependency and SDK layer reuse independent of the publishing workflow.

Use CP YAML 2.0.0 with `agentPool: public/prod-v2-public`, `resourcesPolicy: none`, and `buildkit-custom@3.0.0`. Configure a generic Webhook as a start signal with no branch or commit parameters and no bound GitHub code source. Configure registry authentication through the console-generated `loginCredential` structure. Do not commit credentials or require separate CR username/password environment variables for command steps.

Register `main-head.yml` under CP Template Market > Step Templates before importing the pipeline. A registered custom step has the identifier `custom@1.0.0/{step}@{version}`. Declare `commitSha` in the custom step's `outputs` and write its value to `/tekton/results/commitSha_${CP_STEP_NAME}`. The task exports `commitSha_main-head`, and its dependent task references `$(stages.build-and-push.tasks.resolve-main.outputs.commitSha_main-head)`. CP's preset `exec@1.0.0` has no outputs; declaring a task output cannot extend that component. See the [custom-step output example](https://docs.volcengine.com/docs/cp/Deliver_pipeline_artifacts_through_the_output_of_custom_steps?lang=zh) and [component identifier format](https://docs.volcengine.com/docs/cp/CreateComponentStep?lang=zh).

Resolve `refs/heads/main` once with `git ls-remote`, then use that output for both the shallow Git fetch and the image tag. Pass the SHA through the upstream task's output rather than assuming separate tasks share checkout files. Keep checkout, BuildKit, and cleanup in the same downstream task to share its workspace. The public pool has an older Git: use `git init`, `git fetch --depth=1`, and `git checkout --detach`; do not use `git clone --no-tags`. Use Bash for command execution and an image containing Bash and Git for the custom step. Let Git and BuildKit report errors without extra existence, credential, SHA-format, or digest checks.

Keep the full fetched repository as the build context, build the root Dockerfile's `runtime` stage, and export the final `imageOutput_buildkit-custom` task output. The image defaults to `/bin/bash`, so service deployments must override its startup command. Registering the custom step and configuring actual registry credentials are required before running CP; repository edits alone do not perform those console operations.
